title: Evals config-change regression playbook + routed alert tiers for Console
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a concise playbook and Console integration that surfaces quality regressions caused by model or inference config changes, route alerts to the right operational tiers (Slack -> PagerDuty), and reduce noisy duplicates. This ticket defines the UX, alerting rules, dedupe semantics, and a safe rollout plan so platform teams can detect and act on degradations within SLO windows.

Scope:
- Define evaluation signal set to tie to a code/config/model change (diffed evals vs. baseline).
- Add an 'Evals Regression' alert type in Console with configurable thresholds and severity mapping.
- Implement alert routing rules: Slack for triage, PagerDuty for oncall escalation for high-severity or sustained regressions.
- Deduping strategy: single alert per (change_id, model, metric, dataset) during a sliding window with exponential backoff and a clear mute/unmute control in Console.
- Provide an incident playbook snippet in Console ('What to check') that surfaces recent commits, model versions, prompt set diffs, and a quick rollback/canary link.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Full automation of rollback (will be a follow-up).
- Multi-tenant billing impact calculations.

Rationale:
Customers have reported noisy eval alerts when teams iterate on configs (batching, quantization) that cause transient metric shifts. Engineering needs a deterministic way to surface only actionable regressions and route them to the right responder. This will reduce toil and mean-time-to-detect for regression-related incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Console has a new Evals Regression alert type with UI to configure thresholds per-metric and per-model
Alert routing supports selecting Slack channel and PagerDuty service; mapping rules based on severity are persisted per-project
Deduping de-duplicates alerts that share (change_id, model, metric, dataset) within a 60-minute sliding window by default; setting is configurable
An on-call PagerDuty alert is created for severity=high or if the regression persists past configurable duration (default 15 minutes)
Playbook link and a quick view of related artifacts (recent PRs, model diffs, failing prompt examples) are visible from the alert panel
Unit/integration tests for dedupe logic and routing mappings exist and pass in CI
Documentation added to Confluence and a short Console tooltip guides PM/Eng on how to mute a change or snooze alerts
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flag behind `evals_regression_alerts` for internal teams (redwood-infra, runtime, platform) - 2 weeks
Phase 1: progressive rollout to 10 pilot customers (opt-in) and collect false-positive rate and triage time - 2 weeks
Phase 2: enable by default for accounts with Dedicated tiers; add admin controls in org settings - 1 week
Phase 3: GA with docs and an external migration guide - target release console-2026.04
monitoring_and_alerting_spec: Metric set: per-eval metric (accuracy, hallucination-rate, rouge, custom scoring) reported as change-from-baseline (absolute delta and z-score)
Thresholds: support both absolute delta and percentile drop; default P1: delta > 5% OR z-score < -2; P0/high: delta > 10% OR z-score < -3
Deduping: group key = `${change_id}|${model_id}|${metric}|${dataset_id}`; default window = 60m; repeated alerts escalate backoff: 60m, 3h, 24h
Routing rules: severity=low -> Slack channel only; severity=medium -> Slack + email to owners; severity=high -> Slack + PagerDuty with urgent=true
Sustained-failure trigger: if metric remains degraded across N consecutive eval runs (default N=3), promote to next severity and page oncall
Mute controls: Console UI must allow muting by change_id or model for a specified duration; muting must create an audit log entry with actor and TTL
Audit & metrics: record alert counts, dedupe reductions, time-to-ack, and postmortem link if opened
